utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Good afternoon to you. Mr. Oric, good afternoon. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon. You may be seated. Appearances, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and also good afternoon to my learned colleagues of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with Ms. Joanne Richardson and our acting case manager, Ms. Sanja Bokulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good afternoon to you. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I appear with Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us our assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you, Madam, as well, and your team. I hope there are no preliminaries so that we can proceed with bringing the witness in and try to recover the lost time which I apologise for that. It's not our fault. Neither is it yours. It's just the previous Trial Chamber having had to sit beyond their time limit. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, on that subject, we know we are all going to be very pressed for time today. Myself, certainly, I have a lot of material to get through. Yesterday I was 40 minutes. So I have an hour and 50 minutes left. I would be grateful for an indication of the schedule today, so I know when I'll need to finish, when we will be sitting until, breaks, and also to know, or just to be reassured that I will have time for re-examination on top of that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will try to accommodate you both to the maximum even to the expense of not putting questions ourselves unless it is absolutely necessary. That we promise. Have you tried to inquire whether we will have one break or two breaks? If you can find out from the gentleman in particular. It's okay for him. So we could work out with one break of 30 minutes, and that would be at 4.00. It would be at 4.00. So basically, you have ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, an hour, 45 minutes. It will be 4.15. At 4.15. Or whenever you tell me to stop actually. I mean, because at -- on this, I wouldn't like to impose anything. But let's work on the assumption that we will have one break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mustafic.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As with yesterday we need to get through a lot of material quite quickly, so if you could answer in as few words as possible that would be very helpful, firstly. And secondly, I'm going to continue to use the term "your staff" to refer to the Srebrenica municipality Territorial Defence staff in Tuzla as I did yesterday, again to save time. So I hope that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you were telling us how in July 1992 your staff requested to be -- offered to put yourself at the disposal of the Tuzla District Staff. Did Hazim Sadic of the Tuzla District Staff call to you a meeting after he received your request?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And had you had a meeting with him before then?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was only after that I met with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you explain why you didn't have a meeting before July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I indicated earlier, as of the 22nd of July we were admitted into the TO District Staff and only afterwards did we have meetings which included other Municipal Staffs in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so the meeting with Hazim Sadic, when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably a couple of days after the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And what did you discuss in that meeting with Hazim Sadic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that meeting, Mr. Sadic was interested in knowing, first of all, whether we had any information about the situation in Srebrenica, and about what should the competence of our staff in Tuzla be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What did you understand from that? Did Sadic and the Tuzla District Staff know about the situation in Srebrenica in July 1992, in terms of organs established, staff, what was happening in terms of fighting, or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He most certainly did not, and that is why he thought that we had some information and he wanted us to present at the meeting whatever we knew, which meant that they definitely did not know what was happening in Srebrenica as communications did not function.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You've answered my next question as the reasons for their ignorance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit P29 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this is dated 28 May 1992. And it says "district staff of Territorial Defence Tuzla." In the top right-hand corner you'll see it says "military secret, confidential." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I also want to ask you about the top left-hand corner, the stamp refers to the socialistic republic Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know why they were still using in Tuzla that out-of-date stamp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. Now, first, with this exhibit, I want to you look at the map you marked yesterday, which is D945, if the witness could be shown that, please. And do you recall yesterday you marked places on the map which were -- which appeared in a document, which was P236? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if that could be placed on the ELMO, please. You've marked Tuzla, Zivinice, Lukavac, Gracanica, Palaca, Gradacac and Banovici, and you told us they were all in the immediate Tuzla area; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Srebrenica was not on that list and so you haven't marked it. I'm going to ask you actually if you can now mark Srebrenica with a different pen, with, for example, a yellow highlighter because I believe you used pink. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to move the map or zoom out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now was Srebrenica physically connected to Tuzla at the end of May 1992? Was it possible to -- let me leave it that way.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, does Srebrenica have anything in common with the other places you've marked in pink on that map?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But Srebrenik on the other hand was on the list of yesterday and it's on the map; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at P29 and see at the bottom of the list delivered to, do you see that Srebrenik does not appear on that list?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably instead of Srebrenica written herein, there should be Srebrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's a mistake, in other words. It should say Srebrenik on that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my objection is this document was not authored by this individual, and for Mr. Jones to ask him if it was a mistake, that -- which is why it wasn't there, I think that this witness isn't competent to answer that question. He can only say what he said before with respect to where Srebrenica is located, et cetera, but as it stands here, I don't think he is the appropriate witness to put that question to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's an opinion that he is giving. I mean, he was asked why in his opinion Srebrenik does not appear on the list and he is saying that probably it's there but it's -- there is a mistake. It's not Srebrenica, it's Srebrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Precisely that's his opinion. I'm elaborating on his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For whatever it's worth. It's his opinion. I mean, that I know he didn't author the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: For whatever it's worth indeed, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's the submission on the weight to be given to this evidence. Of course someone who hasn't authored a document can explain why it's a mistake. And I'll demonstrate it further. Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, firstly do you have other reason for thinking that this is a mistake, apart from what you've said about Srebrenik not being in that list and Srebrenica appearing there instead? Can you think of any other reason why it would be a mistake for Srebrenica to be listed there in this document dated 28 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other reason is the very date, 28 May 1992. Because it was on the 22nd July that we were admitted to the District Staff of the Territorial Defence, which shows that at this particular date, this document was not intended for Srebrenica or, rather, for the Srebrenica municipal TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And just to deal with this further, if P29 could be removed from the witness, but we have clean copies of P29 and P236 because we want the witness to mark them. So if he could be passed up -- and I'll show the -- show how I want it passed up -- if you could just put it on the ELMO like this. It's just for the witness because, of course, we've all got our own copies of P29 and P236. If those could be placed on the ELMO in the way that I've given them to the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now what I'm going to ask you to do, Mr. Mustafic, is if you take a pen, just an ordinary writing pen, and I'm going to read if you don't have one -- one is being passed to you -- first I'm going to read from P29 and you tic off the places on the document on the right. So, Banovici, Gracanica, you've done Gracanica, Kalesija, Kladanj, Lukovac, Celic, Tuzla, Zivinice. Now, if you could just circle Srebrenik since that's -- just circle. Circle it, please. And then working the other way, on the document on the left, if you can do the same exercise, first of all, Banovici, underline it. The document on the left. Left. Banovici, Gracanica, Gradacac, Kalesija, Kladanj, Lukavac, Celic -- my apologies, somehow we have got the same that's the English version. My apologies. There has been a slight mistake. We can -- apologies. That was a mistake. We will start again with P29. If I can see again from the usher, the other document. It's no great disaster. We can correct it. My apologies, I must have -- don't know what I was doing. It's okay. We can resume. I thought there was something fishy there. My apologies also to you, Mr. Mustafic. If we can again get the documents next to each other. Now, yes, I think we are okay now. Now, if you -- reading from the document on the right and I'll ask you to underline the documents on the left, Banovici, on the left again, please. Banovici, Gracanica, Gradacac, Kalesija, Lukavac. Celic is not there so you can skip that. Srebrenik is not there. Tuzla, Zivinice, right. So now I'd like you on that document if you could circle Srebrenica. Then actually to correct now, looking at the document from the right to the left, the document on the right has Celic and Kladanj which do not appear on the document on the left. So if you could circle Kladanj and Celic on the document on your right, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Good. Now we've completed that. So as far as the document on the left is concerned, that's P29, that's the odd one out, isn't it, Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, the document on the left is dated May 1992. If Srebrenica is indeed a mistake and Srebrenik should have been written instead, then the list is identical, is it not, apart from Celic and Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation for why the municipal TO staff for those two places, Celic and Kladanj, should be mentioned in a document from July 1992 but not in one from May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that some of the Municipal Staffs were established at specific time periods, and as they established themselves, so they became members of the district TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, and in your opinion, with all of what you know from that period, is there any possibility that the document on the left, P29, from the 28th of May 1992, really refers to Srebrenica and not to Srebrenik?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on that subject I'd like to direct your attention to the first paragraph of this document which you have in front of you. And it says: "On the basis of the code of behaviour of soldiers of the TO, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as our information about faults of the units, improper behaviour and actions in combat of a certain number of TO soldiers in the territory of Tuzla, OKSTO, District Staff, Territorial Defence." Now, if Srebrenik is read for Srebrenica, if those two last letters are wrong, it should be a "k" instead of a "ca," for all those places listed mentioned in this document, were they on the territory of the Tuzla District Staff TO on that date?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But if we read Srebrenica, then there is something odd, since that was not in the territory of the Tuzla District Staff TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Srebrenica is not there because the date here is the 10th of July, and I said that it was on the 22nd of July that the Municipal Staff of Srebrenica was established and joined the District Staff in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thanks. Do you know whether later the district of Tuzla was formed and to include Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And sorry if the witness could be shown Exhibit D282, Defence Exhibit D282. And this is the Official Gazette, 13th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I want to direct your attention to Article 6, which is on the first page of the Bosnian on the right-hand towards the bottom, 6.6. And English, it's page 2. And do you see there that the Tuzla district with its seat in Tuzla encompassing the municipalities of and Srebrenica is listed there, as well as Srebrenik? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And does that conform with your understanding of the situation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's all right. That's fine. I'm finished with that exhibit. Now, was it possible to send documents between Srebrenica and Tuzla after late May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What contacts did you have with Srebrenica after May 1992, in other words, from June 1992 onwards, what contacts, if any?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had several contacts over amateur radio operators.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And with whom did you communicate in Srebrenica via the radio amateurs?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, I contacted family members and the War Presidency of Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the names of the people of the War Presidency with whom you spoke?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Avdic, Mr. Osman Suljic, and Mr. Fahrudin Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And what did you discuss with the War Presidency? What issues on the ham radio?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We communicated over the radio, so they would mostly inquire after their family members, distant and close relatives, who happened to be in the area, that's to say, on the territory of the Tuzla canton.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was this a regular contact?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not regular, but we contacted when necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was the connection made directly to Srebrenica from Tuzla or indirectly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was an indirect connection via the radio amateurs in Zivinice and then via the KFOR -- IFOR.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't certain about the last part the witness mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you repeat the last thing of what you mentioned? We are talking about 1992, the indirect connection via the radio amateurs in Zivinice, what else did you say about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only access we had was via a ham radio set in Zivinice, so these ham amateurs in Srebrenica would establish a connection with those in Zivinice and as there was the possibility to place a call from Zivinice to a family that was there, they would join the -- they would take the telephone receiver and try to link up and establish a connection that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And what you're talking about the telephone receiver between Zivinice, are you talking about between Zivinice and Tuzla or between Zivinice and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Zivinice and Tuzla. Since the telephone lines were operational only on the territory of the Tuzla canton.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you ever transmit military information over the radio amateurs, the ham radio?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We saw a document earlier today, P29, which stated military secret, confidential, on the top right-hand corner. Did you ever broadcast the contents of documents like that on an open line over the ham radio?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. These were military secrets, confidential documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Exhibit P118? This is dated 27 July 1992, it's from the District Staff Tuzla, apparently signed by Hazim Sadic. And it says organisation of courier lines of communication order. And given the shortness of time, I'm not going to read this in any detail, apart from the first paragraph: "Courier lines to deliver mail between the Tuzla district OS staff and Municipal Staffs should be organised according to the diagram attached to this order. Courier lines should be organised as follows." And then we see courier line 1, courier line 2, courier line 3. And if we go to number 4, it says: "The following shall ensure that their couriers remain in daily contact with the district OS staff." And there is a list of places and Srebrenica Opstinski Stab Odbrane OS is mentioned there. Does that refer to communication within Tuzla or to Srebrenica as well? To the territory of Srebrenica as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Solely within Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: At this time, in July 1992, how many kilometres of enemy lines lay between Srebrenica and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was it an easy journey back and forth between Srebrenica and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Far from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was it even possible for couriers from Srebrenica to remain in daily contact with Tuzla staff, running back and forth across 80 kilometres of enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would be a ridiculous thing to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And what is the Srebrenica Opstinski Stab Odbrane OS referred to in this paragraph? Which staff is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff with its headquarters in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did your staff in Tuzla directly communicate with couriers in the Tuzla district at this time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It communicated regularly because we were in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And how did that in fact work, just on a daily basis? Did people go back and forth between your staff in Rudarska Street in the district centre or what?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People went to the district secretariat and the district TO staff to take over the mail and bring it to the headquarters of our Municipal Staff in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And to you, when you see the term courier, does that have any special meaning to you, or does it simply refer to a human being using his legs to go back and forth between two or more places?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A courier in our parts designates a person who went on foot to the institutions I've mentioned and came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I want to go back for a moment to paragraph 3B of this document where it says, it refers to OS staffs in Bratunac, it says Memici and Zvornik, Sapna village. Do you know where Memici is first of all?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't know if you still have the map with you but if so, could you mark it, please, on the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Actually with an M, if you could put an M with the pen.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And at that time, what connection did Memici have with Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, a large number of refugees from Bratunac were accommodated on the territory of Kalesija municipality and specifically in the village of Memici or, rather, in the local commune of Memici which was part of the Tuzla district. That's where they were accommodated and they set up a staff there, and they had communications was Kalesija municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was this a similar setup to your staff in Tuzla but for Bratunac, a staff in Memici for the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The situation was the same. The only difference was that we went to Tuzla and they were in Kalesija.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with that exhibit. Now, did there come a time in 1992 when some people arrived in Tuzla from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was towards the end of October, a group of lads arrived from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did anyone bring a letter for you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And what was the contents of that letter?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that letter, it said that the War Presidency was giving certain rights to a certain number of people in Tuzla to perform certain tasks linked to Srebrenica and the people of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you among those people or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And who signed that letter?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Avdic, the president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know whether any of those people tried to go back to Srebrenica afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of them, Mr. -- the late Salan Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, can you repeat the name, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Salan Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hate to interrupt. Just for clarification for the record, I note there has been reference to people in Tuzla acting on behalf of the people for Srebrenica. Perhaps we can have some information about which people is the -- you know, exactly who Mr. Mandzic is within the context of the people. Just for clarification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's a [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was it just one person who tried to go back to Srebrenica or was it a group of people who tried to return to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did they succeed? Did they all succeed in returning to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were killed in the area of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you repeat the name of the place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ruzina Voda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in the area of Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to come back to that too. But going back to this letter and these representatives, firstly did you then work as a representative for the Srebrenica War Presidency in Tuzla as a result of that letter?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. As a result of receiving that letter, did you work as a representative for the Srebrenica War Presidency but in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did anyone else act as a representative of the Srebrenica War Presidency in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list included Mr. Dzemo Hasanovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you also mentioned a Salan Mandzic. Did he act as a representative or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Salan Mandzic, Dzemo Hasanovic and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, in fact, due to the shortness of time, I'm not going to pursue their functions in detail. Ms. Richardson can do that in cross-examination. Did you receive instructions, however, from the Srebrenica War Presidency about how to do that job of representing the War Presidency in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it all had to do with humanitarian aid for the people who were there, finding accommodation, food, clothing, footwear, and everything else that was necessary for the people who were in Tuzla at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But after receiving this letter of appointment, did you after that receive instructions from Srebrenica itself about how to do your job?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know why not, why that was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was no opportunity to communicate that to me, since there was no means of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. With the usher's assistance if the witness could please be shown D664? This is a document headed "Murat Efendic, Sarajevo," and then an address and it's re application for SDA membership. And he says: "I hereby apply for membership in your party and give the following personal details." It mentions his birth date and place of birth. And then: "I have been a member of the War Presidency of the Srebrenica Municipal Assembly since 2 September 1992," pursuant to a certain decision. Do you know or did you hear of Murat Efendic being a representative of the Srebrenica War Presidency but based in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Murat Efendic for the most part did the same work that I was doing in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. The last sentence of this document he says: "If you find it appropriate, you may grant me retroactive membership from an earlier date." Now, are you familiar with that phenomenon in Bosnia during the war of people being granted retroactive membership in organs, in this case it's the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it was a constant practice in our part, in relation to many things, including membership in the SDA, membership in the army, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you explain a bit more how that happened in the army? I take it you mean the ABiH. Is that something which occurred in relation to Srebrenica, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, when Srebrenica fell, when it was necessary to prove one's membership in the ABiH, quite simply, the date of joining the army was entered retroactively. The dates and the names of certain units were entered according to the wishes of the person entering them, so I am fully aware of the meaning of the term retroactively.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. There's a new exhibit which we will distribute, copies were distributed to the Prosecution yesterday of our new exhibits. It's army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 2nd Corps command, dated 13 November 1992, Tuzla, instructions for application of the rules of the international law of war in the armed forces of the RBiH, and it's signed 2nd Corps commander, Zeljko Knez. Firstly, in fact, did you provide this document to us?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, in Bosnian we see the words [B/C/S spoken]. I think we might need to correct the English. What does that mean, [B/C/S spoken]?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Municipal Staff in Tuzla, of Srebrenica in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Does that mean that it was delivered personally to the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would this document have been delivered through the courier system in Tuzla that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Let me put it this way: Did your staff receive this document in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was that in your capacity as the Municipal Staff to Territorial Defence for Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, I mean the Srebrenica Municipal Defence Staff which was headquartered in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Tuzla, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you disseminate this to Srebrenica? Did you forward it on to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you explain the reason or reasons for why not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reasons are that there was no possibility of doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's the next number, Registrar, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D946, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D946. And this document consists of five pages in Serbo-Croat and the corresponding translation thereof also consisting of five pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm asking if the witness can be shown Exhibit D667, which is dated 23 January 1993. First I just want to note for the record there is no disagreement, that OPSO, Srebrenica, is written in handwriting on the original. Normally in the English it says "handwritten" but it doesn't in this case. So I mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if could you look carefully at this document, Mr. Mustafic and answer this: Was this the same situation as you've already described, in other words, this document being received by your staff in Tuzla, or was it a different situation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same. This document was received by our staff in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was it sent to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was that for the same reasons that you've already mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in the interests of time, I won't ask the witness to repeat on each occasion why it wasn't forwarded. I've finished with that exhibit. If the witness could be shown Exhibit D674 now, please? And this is dated 22 July 1993, and it says "Decision". My apologies, one moment. Yes. Well, it's forwarded by Commander Hazim Sadic and, yes, below it says decision about a change of the rules of service in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And again the same question, really: Was this received by your staff in Tuzla or by some other staff when we see that it was sent to OPSO Municipal Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff of Srebrenica in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And besides these few documents we have looked at, were there other documents and rules which you received from the Tuzla district TO staff and from other organs?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And before demilitarisation, did you transfer any of them to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Had we wanted to, we would not have been able to. There was no possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document. Are you familiar with the packet communication system? Yes, are you familiar with the packet communication, that term?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Packet communications, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When did you become aware of the packet communications system in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The packet system began to function after the demilitarisation of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And once this system began to function, did you have direct access to it? Were you able to use it whenever you wished?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was within the competence of the command of the 2nd Corps and they issued decisions on when and where someone could use the packet system.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you able to send long documents through the packet system?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And again why not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because the packet system with Srebrenica was difficult to maintain because in Srebrenica there was a shortage of power. The system would often break down. They were unable to get spare parts. So it was only used when absolutely necessary, and the length of the text would be only a few sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you in fact try to send documents of more than one page to Srebrenica using the packet system?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't even try, because Srebrenica was a demilitarised zone and communications functioned only for exchanges of information about families, about the situation of people's families, whether they had accommodation, whether they had food to eat and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now going back now before demilitarisation, you've told us about this group of people, some of whom at least were killed trying to go back in the Han Pijesak area. Can you tell us first how large the group was which was trying to get to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: How many were killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit P154, please. This is dated 27 November 1992. And it says, again [B/C/S spoken] It's not in English. Do you agree? Do you see on right-hand corner [B/C/S spoken]?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I think you may also agree that in the Bosnian, we don't actually see the word "telegram" in full but in English it appears as telegram. But supposing the word is indeed telegram, was it possible to send telegrams from or between Tuzla and Srebrenica in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read the second paragraph: "You know that a group of defenders from Srebrenica managed to reach the free territory in Tuzla via Vlasenica and Kladanj municipalities a month ago." Pausing there, a month ago would be October 1992. Is this the group that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Then it says: "The Srebrenica Municipal Staff of the armed forces with headquarters in Tuzla with the help of the command of the 2nd Corps provided equipment and ammunition to the extent that they could, a unit from Srebrenica has been in the Nezuk sector since 3 September 1992 and joined the preparations for a breakthrough on insertion to the free territory of Srebrenica via the Zvornik and Bratunac area," et cetera. Now, firstly, when there is this reference to the Srebrenica Municipal Staff of the armed forces, again, is that your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you involved in these plans?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then we see the order and it says: "The commands of the OG 4," Operations Group "in Kalesija and the OG 3 in Kladanj and the Srebrenica Municipal Defence Staff will immediately carry out a detailed valuation of the situation in order to urgently find a way of sending certain quantities of ammunitions and PO equipment to the Srebrenica free territory along the axes mentioned." Again, I suppose it's an obvious question, but is this your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now if we turn to the second page and we see that this is to be forwarded to Srebrenica Opstina Stab OS, again your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's also to be forwarded to the commander of the Srebrenica unit in Nezuk. Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a unit that was located in Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know -- yes, I'll ask actually you to mark that on a map in a moment. Yes, if you could mark Nezuk on the map, please. With an N, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you actually know the name of the person who was the commander much that unit in Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you answer, because I want to avoid any confusion, the witness did mark an N next to a cross or an X that he put at 40 minutes to the -- to Banja Koviljaca and above the previously marked M and K. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, of course. One moment, Mr. Jones. Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I just have problems to follow. Did I understand you correctly that you have been involved in drafting this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Not the order. I was involved in organising the group that was supposed to go to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know the name of the commander of the Srebrenica unit which was in Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Salih Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did he make it to Srebrenica or was he one of the ones that was killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was among those who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of page 1 in the English there is a reference to a meeting to be held at the 2nd Corps command on the 1st of December 1992, which among others, the Srebrenica Opstinski Stab SO commander was to be present. Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were Salih Salihovic and the commander of OG 4 also present?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Mr. Salihovic and Mr. Efendic, the commander of the 4th Operations Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you've told us that 64 of these people were killed in this group. Were they all fighters or were there other people among them?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Among them were two doctors. They were medical staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were they killed or did they survive?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you involved in trying to get the bodies retrieved of the killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We have a new exhibit to distribute on that subject. And this is headed Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Srebrenica SO War Presidency, representative office in Tuzla, Tuzla, 22 November 1994. And it's a report on the exchange in Satorovici of bodies of persons killed and the forensic medical findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Look at this document. Firstly, did you prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And does this refer to the same group of 64 killed who you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through the group for exchange we insisted that an exchange of the bodies of the persons killed at Ruzina Voda be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was there a pathological report prepared in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This information was drawn up after the pathological report was drawn up, at Gradina in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did it show about the people who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were brought in makeshift wooden coffins. When I insisted that these coffins be opened up to see whether they contained corpses at all, the side of Republika Srpska did not permit the coffins to be opened at first. However, we insisted, and I opened several of the coffins. I saw a horrific sight. The people mostly had their hands tied behind their backs with wire and three of them were without heads. Their heads were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did the fact that -- or did this event and other events have any effect on the willingness of people to try to reach Srebrenica from Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every such event definitely discouraged people from any such attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The Prosecution has suggested and may suggest to you that Naser Oric should have gone to Tuzla before demilitarisation for training. I'll quote what they've said in that regard. "There was, however, for him, Oric, available a training centre in Tuzla. He didn't make use of it. Didn't make use of it."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm not sure this is an appropriate way to ask a question on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him put the question and answer. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know what he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I know. And so do I, Your Honour. But I think the question can be posed with the suggestion without quoting something that the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no suggestion as yet. Let him finish the question and then if it's necessary I will intervene. But he hasn't even finished the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is it a realistic suggestion that Naser Oric should have gone to Tuzla for training? And in case there is any confusion, the suggestion is that Naser Oric could or should have travelled through 80 kilometres of enemy territory, minefields, et cetera, in which you had told us people had been killed, beheaded, to attend a training seminar and then go back the end of it? Is that a realistic suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speechless, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I take it you don't think that that is a realistic suggestion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's obvious, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If the witness in fact could be shown Exhibit D673, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't given it a number as yet. This last document that you used with the witness, Judge Eser is drawing my attention that we haven't given it a number as yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So this document, which consists of two pages, without an ERN, two pages in Bosnian, Serbo-Croat, and the two pages in English, being a translation of the original, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D947.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, D673 is dated 30 June 1993. And it's army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 2nd Corps command, Tuzla, 30 June 1993. "In order to realise the direct tasks following from the obligation to respect and ensure the application of the law of war under all conditions, I hereby order..." and then it's for a training seminar to be held, and it's signed Hazim Sadic. Are you aware of the 2nd Corps organising seminars?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And when we see at the bottom, to Opstinski Stab, OPSO, does that -- does that relate to your staff in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To our staff in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was this invitation forwarded to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you -- did your staff actually participate in seminars?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You didn't have to go through minefields or enemy territory to get there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, even so, sometimes it proved difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned people who came from Srebrenica in October 1992 or from that area. Did you speak to him about -- did you speak to them about how fighting was organised, if it was organised, in that area in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to many people who arrived, especially when they had to be deported in UN trucks where they had to pass the journey on their feet, children, women and elderly alike. They were telling me that the chaos ruled over there. There was -- everything was in total disarray. There was no organisation there, which was the reason why the events unfolded as they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You mentioned people being deported in UN trucks. Are you aware whether any people died while being so deported?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were so many of them boarded on the trucks that some of them even choked as they were on their way to freedom, toward Tuzla canton. Some of them even suffocated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving to a slightly different area, do you know Edhem Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he was on the Bratunac Municipal Staff based in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit D822, please. And this is -- it says on the top Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Drina division command, and it appears to be signed by the commander of the Drina division, Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I want you just to peruse this document and see the mention of some names there. There's a Sead Djozic. Do you know the Sead Djozic referred to in this document? It's at number 3.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sead Djozic also worked in the Bratunac Municipal Staff based in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know the Kelvedin Djozic referred to in this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And who was he and what was he doing in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also a member of the staff. He was an active member of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When we look at the top of this document it's addressed to Mr. Ahmic. Do you know who that referred to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Edhem Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. This document refers to in one place an order of 9 September 1992 and to preparations to go to the free territory by 30 September 1992. Does it or does it not seem right to you, also in light of your own knowledge of events mentioned here, whether this document was composed between the 9th and the 30th of September 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if we are now getting into an area of speculation. If what's being asked of this witness is based on the contents, when this letter would have been composed, I think that any answer from the witness at this point is pure speculation. I don't think anything within the context of this letter notwithstanding some dates mentioned when this letter could have been composed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate your concern, Ms. Richardson, but looking again at the question, is -- what's -- it focuses upon is also in the light of your own knowledge of the events mentioned here. So at that stage, if he can answer the question, he will answer it. If he in answering -- trying to answering it, he believes that he will be just speculating, I don't want an answer from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I do appreciate your concerns, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Witness, Mr. Mustafic, we don't want speculation from you. I mean, please listen carefully to what Mr. Jones is asking from you and try to answer your question to the best of your ability based on your knowledge. If you are not in a position to answer it, if you're just guessing, then, tell us, "I can only guess, so I prefer not to answer the question." Did I make myself clear? I think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I did because this is an intelligent witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I say, Your Honour, I'm really making all the my efforts to go quickly, and I deliberately framed the question in light of your own knowledge of events. I couldn't have been clearer, and I think we've wasted two minutes for nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll approach it in a different way. Do you know Nijaz Dubicic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The interpretation wasn't ... Nijaz Dubicic, yes, could you repeat whether you know him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that his brother Mensur died?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know roughly when that was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late September.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In light of your own knowledge and what you know and only on what you know, don't speculate, any idea when this document would have been composed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know that Nurif Rizvanovic went to the Bratunac area or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found that out only once he had already gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you involved in any planning relating to the attempt by Nurif and his men to get into the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The people we've seen mentioned in this document, Sead Djozic, Kelvedin Djozic, where were they from, what municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this document we have seen, is it to do with Bratunac or is it to do with other municipalities, in terms of the people -- actually, I'll withdraw that. Let me rephrase it. Was Nurif Rizvanovic's trip anything to do with your staff in Tuzla? Were you involved in that in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Incidentally, do you know which municipality the following places are located? Kravica, Jezestica, Bjelovac and Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving to a new subject and new exhibit, actually, sorry, no. It's D656. New exhibit but not a completely new exhibit. This is dated 19 January 1993. It's army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 2nd Corps command, 19 January 1993, Tuzla. Do you recall whether you received this document in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And incidently, looking at the B/C/S version, there is a stamp which I think you can see says "Bratunac" in the top right-hand corner, so I'm referring to not this copy but the order itself.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One cannot really see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. It's not important. Did you send your copy of this order on to Srebrenica, on to the free territory of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was that for the same reasons as before, or for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the same reasons as before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this -- right. Let me put it this way: Did you do anything about this order?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the military police is concerned, we did not have a specific unit of our own and therefore we recruited our soldiers into the military unit of Tuzla in the Buna barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you sent some people along to the district staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, 2nd Corps command. Now, the first paragraph refers to a number of places, Bijeljina, Zvornik. Dealing with Bijeljina, did that fall to the Serbs at some stage, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijeljina fell right at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So whether we see the reference in paragraph 1, the Municipal Defence Staffs, and then a number of places are referred to, including Srebrenica, does this again refer to Municipal Defence Staffs in exile in the Tuzla area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This here contains information about all the Municipal Staffs who were in exile in Tuzla, because the population of the Podrinje area was mostly to be found in the territory of the Tuzla district. It included, among others, those from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now if you could keep that document, and if the witness could be shown D649, please. And in particular, I'd just like to put the two stamps next to each other on the ELMO. And it's, yes, a question of having the two stamps next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I know you said, Mr. Mustafic, that you had difficulty seeing the -- seeing the stamps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just allow me one moment, please. It should be D656 and D649.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that the first one is 656. I think it's 646. I stand to be corrected but I have got that impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That one is correct. I see, it's a question of the stamp. It's the stamp on the top right-hand corner, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do we have the right documents to start with?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes,.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You're happy with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There we go. That's what I was after.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if you look at those two stamps, would you agree or disagree that they are the same stamp, the same -- the details are obviously different but the same stamp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so looking -- you can put D656 to one side and just look at the one on the left, D649, this document dated 29th November 1992, dealing with Bratunac, signed by the chief of the Municipal Staff, Bratunac municipality, is this a staff in the Tuzla area, or is it a staff in the Bratunac free territory?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with those exhibits and we have a new exhibit dated 30 January 1993. This is the number, reference number is 13-193, Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Defence, district secretariat of Defence, subject joint meeting to gain insight into the work of the municipal secretariats of Defence in Tuzla district. Did you provide us with this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the contents?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did your staff or not have meetings with the Tuzla District Staff secretariat?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this document appears to be signed by Fuad Hadziavdic. Do you know who that would be?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's the secretary of the secretariat for national defence in the district.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. On that second page, there is reference to a meeting on the 17th of February 1993 in Zivinice and Srebrenica municipal secretariat of Defence is to attend as well. Did anyone from your staff attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Husein Efendic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When did he join your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Year, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document which consists of one page in B/C/S and two pages in English, no ERN, is being tendered and is being marked as Defence Exhibit D948.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now if the witness could please be shown D669, Defence Exhibit D669. This is dated 29 April 1993. It's an order - I'm just doing this for the record to save time - "All municipal secretariats that send recruits, conscripts for training to the training centres in Tuzla, Smoluca, and Dubrave ordered to provide a sufficient quantity of meals for their recruits for each day of training." This concerns a training -- obviously it's signed by Fuad Hadziavdic and it's addressed to, among others, all municipal secretariats for defence in the Tuzla district.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recall the events described here or the training described here?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The recruits had to be provided with clothes, food, and other items which we found very difficult but we had to do it. That's why I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So did your staff send people for this training?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's sufficient for that document. We have a new exhibit, which is dated 19 May 1993. This next document is Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Tuzla District Assembly, dated 19 May 1993, and it says: "With regard to your communication number" -- number is given -- "of 16 May 1993, we would like to inform you that as regards the problem of Srebrenica the Presidency of Tuzla District Assembly has so far had contact with Tuzla CSB, the army of the Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina, 2nd Corps command, and Mr. Mirsad Mustafic, who was introduced as the representative of Srebrenica SO in Tuzla. Please inform us whether we will continue to have contact with this gentleman or if you will appoint a new representative." Can you explain what this is about, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically from the War Presidency of Srebrenica, in view of the fact that there was no communication, they didn't know what the situation was like in Tuzla, and we didn't know what the situation was like in Srebrenica. Under such circumstances, they asked from the president of the Municipal Assembly of the district, Hadzic, to allow them to deal with all the matters relating to Srebrenica, and here it is stated that they have contacts with the CSB in Tuzla, with the command of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's economise on time. Two pages, one B/C/S, one English, D949.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next exhibit will be D677. Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Apparently in the English it's been admitted. Here it is stated that they have contacts with the CSB in Tuzla with the command of the 2nd Corps and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you can confirm, Mr. Mustafic, that that was part of your answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think he needs to confirm it. It emerges from the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's true, that's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, D677 I think has been distributed to you. Did you provide this document to us?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you have document in front of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think he received interpretation, from what I could guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's D677, if you have this document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's simply whether or not you provided this.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if you're able to, can you explain briefly what this is about? And first of all I think a correction needs to be added in Bosnian it's [B/C/S spoken] rather than [B/C/S spoken]. Perhaps the witness could confirm this and tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the -- when package communications started functioning, there was a number of documents that had to be forwarded from the Tuzla district or, rather, from the Presidency of the Tuzla district, which included among others quite voluminous documents. Since we, those of us in the staff, had no means of communication and were unable to forward any documents, this was mostly done through the command of the 2nd Corps. In view of the fact that the Tuzla district forwarded the documentation to us, and in view of the fact that the documentation was quite voluminous, we were unable to do it on our own and we asked Ms. Seada Palavric, who was secretary of the president of the district, Mr. Izet Hadzic, to use her offices to do so because we thought that she would find it easier to forward the documents, since package communication could not be used for forwarding any voluminous documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did this include gazettes, for example?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely. Official Gazettes, anything that had to do with the functioning of the government, of the cantonal authorities and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not Seada Palavric succeeded in delivering the documents to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never received any feedback.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we breaking at 4.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. I'll keep going then.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have a new document, which is dated 21 June 1994. It's the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Tuzla District Presidency, subject implementation of the constitution of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And first can you tell us whether or not you provided us with this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, the second paragraph reads: "Bearing in mind the fact that both Srebrenica and Bratunac are located in the territory which is temporarily physically cut off from the rest of the free territory of Tuzla district, please start applying the constitution in a manner described in the memorandum attached to this letter, attempting to ensure that five delegates from each of you to the cantonal assembly are actually in a position to participate in the work of that assembly in Tuzla." Again, can you explain what this is all about, if you can, briefly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that in view of the fact that Srebrenica, Bratunac and Vlasenica municipalities were all part of the Tuzla canton, when selecting the bodies of government or the assembly or the ministry or anything else, and as the territory was physically separated from the free territory of the district, we had to nominate individuals to be appointed to certain posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you propose delegates and the assembly appointed them?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, we proposed delegates who were on the territory of the canton, who were physically able to attend the sessions, and the cantonal government made the selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. So have I understood correctly in June 1994 Srebrenica municipality was represented in Tuzla by persons proposed by your staff in Tuzla; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. This document, which consists of one page in B/C/S, two pages in English, no ERN, is being tendered and filed as Defence Exhibit D950.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Next Exhibit would be D679.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Firstly, this is fairly lengthy correspondence, but did you or did you not see this document when you were with us in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you recall this correspondence from your own experience? In other words, do you recall the events described here concerning material to be sent to Srebrenica and a question of whether or not it had been received in Srebrenica? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I remember that. These are the materials connected to the making of a seal and they were to be forwarded to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was it also a question of Official Gazettes from 1993 and 1994 being sent in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, can you confirm whether or not the information was received that even by the 24th of March 1995, those materials had not arrived in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if we go past the first page to the other pages which appear to be signed by it says Brigadier Naser Oric, is it correct, do you know, whether or not Naser Oric was asking for and trying to get stamps and ranks and other items sent to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that I received a document like this one requesting -- with a request for seals to be made and sent to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What did you do about it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC [Resumed]
